    UI node

    The UI node is the main screen-state node. It controls registered Views when navigation enters or leaves the node and waits for one of its outputs to choose the next route.

    Node options

    Option Description
    Display Name Label shown on the graph node
    Node Description Authoring note stored with the runtime node
    Clear History Clears Back and Forward stacks after entering this node
    Use Back Allows a Back request on this active node to call Back()
    On Enter UI Show/Hide commands applied when this node becomes active
    On Exit UI Show/Hide commands merged in when leaving this node
    Outputs Dynamic routes originating from this node

    Each Show or Hide command selects a View catalog address and either Animated or Instant mode. Show wins if one navigation change would both Show and Hide the same address.

    Output types

    Type Matching event
    UI Button NavButton click or RequestButtonSignal(...)
    Signal RequestSignal(...) from application code
    Time Delay Unscaled seconds since this node became active
    Toggle NavToggle value change matching On, Off, or Any
    UI View A matching View starts an Animated Show or Hide

    UI View routes react when an Animated transition starts, not when its animation finishes. Instant View commands and InstantShow() or InstantHide() calls do not raise this output.

    Each output can be left unconnected while drafting. Once connected, it must lead to exactly one UI or Action chain. Duplicate Button/Signal addresses, duplicate View conditions, and overlapping Toggle conditions such as Any plus On are validation errors.

    Important

    A NavButton uses the Button catalog and a UI Button output even though its UXML properties are named signal-category and signal-key. A graph Signal output is a different event channel.

    Normal UI outputs are authored as Push transitions. The previous node is pushed only when the connected Action chain reaches another screen; a terminal Action chain only runs its Actions. Use Back controls whether the active node accepts a Back request, not the output's authored transition kind.
